subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: What should OpenClaw do by default when an agent turn emits tool-call-shaped assistant text instead of a structured tool invocation?
rationale: The source shows both warning-only handling and bounded text promotion today, while stricter rejection or forced retry changes the security boundary and local-model compatibility contract.

options.title: Define bounded enforcement
options.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and then implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.

options.title: Keep warning-only compatibility
options.body: Keep current behavior and treat this as documented local-model/provider incompatibility, accepting that fake tool-call text can still reach transcripts or visible replies.

options.title: Split broader claim checks
options.body: Limit this issue to syntactic fake tool-call text and leave natural-language success claims to the broader pre-response or claim-ledger tracking issues.

recommendation.title: Define bounded enforcement
recommendation.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and then implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.
